I believe you can make everything go parabolic in life. It’s just a matter of taking care of the small gains. 

Those gains seem to be negligible in the beginning but if you master the art of small gains, you will soon go parabolic. 

This is the Kaizen philosophy, make sure you improve yourself with 1% everyday. It seems small but if you do this you’ll be x38 times better at the end of the year, x1.444 at the end of year 2. You see the parabolic curve. 

My learning curve in investment started 10 years ago. I invested in low beta companies with paper money. I had no money available to invest with my own money but wanted to be prepared when that day comes. 

I moved from low beta stocks, to dividend stocks, to value stocks, to high growth stocks at the moment. From a paper trader in low beta stocks to the second best investor (behind a certain Serenity) on the platform according to @buzzberg_ai. 

You should try to implement this learning curve in everything you do. Don’t chase the big wins but make the small ones consistent. 

Is it really this easy? 

Off course not, it takes a lot of discipline and focus. 

As I said, your gains will seem negligible. You will have to take small calculated risksk to make sure you keep those daily gains. 

Let me give you kickboxing as an example. You are kicking the opponents thigh 1 time, 2 times, 3 times,… every kick hurts the opponent but with every kick you have to take a calculated risk not to expose yourself. 

Depending on your opponent it can take up to 20 kicks before you start to notice some instability. This can frustrate you, you go for a knock-out, expose yourself and get countered. All those gains for nothing. 

It’s the same with investing, be disciplined. Control your FOMO, you don’t want to lose everything you have build because you take uncalculated risks. 

It seems easy to control this but I’ve played League for a while and here I learned that it’s in the human nature to f* up your smaller gains. Every ones in a while you will throw your gains away and feel frustrated. 

The only thing you can do here is learn from it and move on. There is no future in the past, only lessons to be learned.

4. Advanced Precision Agriculture & Sustainability
Moving beyond basic crop monitoring toward predictive yield analytics and sustainability tracking. By utilizing their high-frequency time-series data, Planet can help global agribusinesses reward farmers for sustainable practices, monitor biodiversity, and track net-zero emission targets across massive agricultural supply chains.

Instead of farmers manually scouting massive fields, Planet's data feeds into John Deere's systems (like the John Deere Operations Center) to provide near real-time insights on crop health, moisture levels, and biomass.

This allows the heavy machinery, such as tractors and sprayers, to apply precise amounts of water, fertilizer, or pesticides only exactly where they are needed, rather than blanket-spraying an entire field.

Something I did not emphasize enough in my $PL deep-dive is how bullish the partnership with $GOOGL is. It's an advantage no other company in the industry has. 

A first hurdle for competitors are the massive amounts of data they need to store. They need a cloud provider to help them store and organize the data. Planet has that in Google. Planet's entre operational pipeline is built on and powered by Google Cloud Platform. It was part of the agreement of the Terra bella acquisition of Planet in 2017. 

Planet is building it's own Large Earth Model (LEMs) and Agentic AI workflows. They partner with Google on this as well, they are leveraging Google's Remote Sensing Foundation Model (RSFM) alongside with Gemini-powered reasoning. This integration is what gives the application its agentic capabilities, allowing it to understand a conversational text prompt, autonomously scan Planet's daily global imagery, detect specific objects or changes over time, and synthesize the findings into an analytic report.

Planet refers to this initiative as Queryable Earth or Planetary Intelligence. Instead of training a model purely on internet text, they are essentially training AI on Earth observation data about the physical world. Google's foundation models provide the underlying architecture that translates the user's natural language into complex geospatial queries.

Early 2026 Google and Planet released the highly experimental Project Suncatcher. This is a research initiative exploring the feasibility of running data-center-style computing systems in low Earth orbit. The project aims to see if near-continuous solar power and the vacuum of space can efficiently support energy-intensive artificial intelligence workloads. Planet is leveraging its manufacturing and operational expertise to build and help deploy two demonstration spacecraft for Google, targeted for launch around 2027.

There is no SaaS space company has this massive advantage. These initiatives will blow up the TAM of Planet.

A lot of investors wondering how to profit form the new NVIDIA's 800V HVDC architecture. $WOLF published a great white paper on why SiC is necessary for the pivot. Here is my summary of the paper:

Next generation AI factories require massive amounts of power. Delivering power at 800V DC reduces wiring requirements, improves efficiency, and allows for mu higher GPU density in server racks. 

However the major bottleneck is getting power from the utility grid to the data center. Currently, this relies on conventional medium-voltage (MV) iron-core transformers, which use heavy copper windings and magnetic cores to step down the AC voltage. The massive spike in AI data center construction has caused a supply chain crisis for these traditional transformers, resulting in lead times of up to 3 years.

To bypass this supply chain bottleneck and improve efficiency, engineers are replacing traditional heavy iron-core transformers with Solid-State Transformers (SSTs).

An SST uses solid-state semiconductor devices (power electronics) rather than just copper coils to step down and convert the voltage. It takes the 13.8 - 35 kV AC power from the grid and directly converts it into the 800 VDC required by the AI server racks.

Conventional power switches made of standard Silicon (specifically, Silicon IGBTs - Insulated-Gate Bipolar Transistors) cannot handle the requirements of an SST effectively. They suffer from high switching losses and are limited to low switching frequencies (a few hundred Hertz).

This is where Silicon Carbide (SiC), a wide-bandgap semiconductor, comes in:

- High Switching Frequency: SiC MOSFETs (Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistors) can operate at frequencies greater than 10,000 Hz.

- Smaller Magnetics: In transformer design, as switching frequency increases, the physical size of the required magnetic coils and cores decreases. By switching at >10,000 Hz, SiC enables compact, lightweight SSTs that take up a fraction of the floor space of a traditional transformer.

- Thermal Efficiency: Wolfspeed’s SiC achieves 99% conversion efficiency, which reduces the need for heavy thermal cooling systems by 50% compared to Silicon IGBTs.

The article highlights two distinct engineering approaches to building an SST, depending on the blocking voltage of the SiC devices used:

1. Medium-Voltage (MV) SiC (< 5kV blocking voltage)

- Architecture: Because the voltage is lower, engineers must use a multi-level architecture comprising several cascaded converter cells (stacking multiple devices in series) to handle the grid's high voltage.

- Pros: Smaller, highly modular building blocks that are easier to service. Commercially available 3.3kV gate drivers already exist. It also generates a smaller dv/dt (the rate of change of voltage over time), which minimizes Electromagnetic Interference (EMI).

- Cons: Requires complex control algorithms to trigger the series of switches perfectly, and demands precise insulation coordination between the cells.

2. High-Voltage (HV) SiC (> 5kV blocking voltage)

- Architecture: Utilizing Wolfspeed’s advanced 10kV SiC MOSFETs, designers can use a much simpler two-level cell architecture.

- Pros: Vastly simplifies the control scheme and insulation needs because there are fewer cascaded cells.

- Cons: These devices switch with a very high dv/dt, which requires an ultra-low-parasitic design to manage EMI. Furthermore, compatible gate drivers for >3.3kV are rare, often requiring custom development.

In short, the article argues that the rapid expansion of AI requires a fundamental redesign of how power is delivered from the grid. By utilizing 10kV SiC MOSFETs to build Solid-State Transformers, the industry can eliminate massive transformer lead times, achieve higher efficiency, and deliver the specific 800V HVDC power that modern AI clusters require, provided the industry can mature the surrounding ecosystem of high-voltage gate drivers and millisecond-class DC fault clearing protection systems.

@red1wj Numbers without context are just numbers and context without numbers is just context. Have learned that only when you combine both, you can draw meaningful conclusions.

I see a lot of people completely misinterpreting this graph, as absolute numbers like this basically say nothing on their own.

First of all there is a difference between backlog and orders on hand (ooh). While American companies only need to report the backlog, the ooh tells much more. Your backlog basically has no timeframe, while your ooh only starts when you receive the purchase order. 

If you sign a 10-year frame agreement, you can put all these orders in backlog. But the customer will place several different purchase orders within this frame agreement, so your ooh will be way smaller and on a shorter timeframe. 

You can have a $1 billion backlog over 10-years with only 5% in ooh but also a $200 million backlog over 1-year with 95% in ooh. 

Secondly, I saw some people putting the backlog against the market cap to see which is the best investment. Even with the ooh, this would be completely useless without considering the margins. 

The SaaS model of $PL has way higher margins than $FLY for example. A lower backlog or ooh can result in higher free cash flow. 

Lastly, backlog is not always a positive thing. It all depends on the predictability of your product. In a production environment a backlog can mean a lot of delays and unhappy customers. 

A subscription on the other hand is very predictable and the backlog will always be converted into revenues. 

So, be careful with taking conclusions out of numbers without knowing any context.
